# Open Port Scanner (open-port-tools/port-scanner)

> Fast, cross-platform open port checker and asynchronous IP network scanner for Windows, macOS, and Linux with GUI and CLI.

## Summary
Open Port Scanner is a zero-dependency open-source utility for discovering open TCP ports, scanning whole local subnets (`--lan` / CIDR `/24`), inspecting TLS certificates, and grabbing service/HTTP banners on Windows, macOS, and Linux. It serves as a lightweight, standalone alternative to Angry IP Scanner, Nmap (Zenmap), and Advanced Port Scanner.

## Key Capabilities
- 1-click local network (`LAN /24`) detection and multi-host scanning.
- Bounded asynchronous worker pool supporting full `1-65535` port sweeps without external drivers or Java.
- Service identification for 120+ well-known ports plus HTTP (`Server`, `<title>`) and TLS certificate inspection.
- Dual mode: desktop GUI (`--gui` / `--web`) and scriptable CLI (`--json`, `-o report.csv|json|md|txt`).
- Pre-built standalone executables for Windows (`.exe`), macOS (`.app`), and Linux via GitHub Releases.

## Quick Commands
- Scan detected local network: `port-scanner --lan --profile quick`
- Check specific ports: `port-scanner <target> -p 22,80,443,8080`
- Full 1-65535 scan: `port-scanner <target> --profile full`
- Launch GUI: `port-scanner --gui`
